rationale: First real firing of the redesigned PERSISTENT-SESSION growth bot (replacing trig_01MzFMv1sC8AAo9UwZkKRNoB's fresh-session-per-fire design, which the previous log entry documents as never once pushing despite reporting success on every firing). Did fresh WebSearch research (last systematic research was 2026-09-14, three weeks prior) into 2026 YouTube Shorts-to-subscriber funnel tactics and category/niche positioning for ambient channels, since the subscriber count has been flat-to-noisy (14 on 9/25 -> ~18 estimated on 9/27 -> 16 confirmed on 10/6) despite the 9/25 and 9/28 changes. Findings: (1) the '3-second hook' and 'cliffhanger/open-loop' Short-to-long conversion techniques researched are primarily about the Short's VIDEO CONTENT/EDIT (what's shown first, a verbal CTA, an unresolved narrative beat) -- not reachable from this bot's strict metadata.js/thumbnail.js/index.js scope, which excludes src/render.js (where Short cutting/duration/fit logic lives); (2) the direct metadata-level version of this technique -- a first-line link from the Short to the full video, plus a subscribe CTA -- was already shipped 2026-09-25 (withFullVideoLink/subscribeUrl in src/metadata.js); (3) 'oddly satisfying' / general ambient-screensaver genre positioning is already covered by existing BASE_TAGS ('satisfying', 'hypnotic visuals', 'trippy visuals', etc.) and the #Shorts/#ambient/#relaxing hashtags already in both descriptions; (4) a category-ID change (currently 24/Entertainment) was considered but the research surfaced no concrete evidence either way for this niche, only vague genre framing -- not a 'clearly worth trying' change per this routine's own bar, just a guess with no way to attribute outcome. Concluded there is no new, well-evidenced, in-scope lever today that isn't already shipped: the 9/25-9/28 changes are still the most recent real content/metadata shift, only 11-15 days of (sparse, noisy) subscriber data has accumulated since, and shipping another speculative tweak now would make it harder, not easier, to eventually tell what the 9/25-9/28 changes actually did. Per this routine's own guidance, skipping is the correct call, not a failure to find something: 'shipping a change on a hunch... pollutes the log's ability to show what's actually working.'
